items.titleEn: “I hope my story can help others”
items.summaryEn: Arsenal helped to fund one of The ACED Project’s Stories Like Ours films
bodyEn: The Arsenal Foundation has helped to fund one of The ACED Project’s Stories Like Ours films, in this case the real-life story of Aaron, who turned his life around after dealing drugs and being stabbed. The three key people behind the film – Les Rowe, Tom Watt and Aaron himself – tell us about it.
Les Rowe is a director of the ACED Project Community Interest Company, under whose umbrella the Stories Like Ours films have been made. He also happens to be Emile Smith Rowe’s father…

“My link to Arsenal in the Community came about via my role as education, employment and training advisor at Independent Future, Islington’s leaving care service. I work closely with the Community team, referring young people for employment and training opportunities. I have taken children to the Street Child World Cup and every year I work Christmas Day at The Arsenal Hub with the Community team and a charity called Go Forward Youth to put on a Christmas lunch for care leavers. I was always keen to keep Emile grounded so he has attended that event as well as our Kick Off homework club at the Hub.

“The ACED Project CIC came about via a chance conversation via LinkedIn during lockdown in 2021 with likeminded people who were keen to support care experienced young people using the power of sport – specifically football. Our aim is for this cohort to Aspire, Collaborate and be Empowered, hence the name. My fellow directors, father and son Bradley and Jack Goldenberg, and I work with a wide range of organisations on projects that aim to inspire young people and help them find employment or gain qualifications.

“Tom and I met in a cafe just across the road from The Arsenal Hub. I was going to watch a youth game at the Emirates and popped in for a coffee. I saw Tom sitting there and thought I would say hi, having recognised him from his role in EastEnders.

“Tom was very engaging, and we sat and chatted football for a while before I revealed why I was at the game. Tom raved about Emile as one of the young players everyone was keeping an eye on. We’ve been in touch ever since and now work closely together on the Stories Like Ours.

“We rely totally on donations to make these films. I was lucky to have a long-term friend sponsor the first film, and a parent of a pre-academy player at The Arsenal Hub sponsored the second. The Arsenal Foundation helped us with the fourth film.”
Tom Watt is the interviewer and director for Stories Like Ours, and has been an Arsenal fan for the best part of 60 years…

“I met Alan Sefton, one of my heroes in football, in 1986, when he arrived at Highbury to take up the role as Arsenal’s first head of community. I’ve been lucky enough to be involved with the Community department ever since, from producing educational materials for the Double Club scheme – which is celebrating its 25th anniversary – to founding Arsenal’s charity football team. It has been a pleasure and a privilege. And now, I’m grateful that The Arsenal Foundation has helped us bring an amazing story to life on film.
“Les and a colleague were setting up The ACED Project and were looking for ideas. I had one: Stories Like Ours. We’ve been working together on them together since.

“I sit down with the subject of each film – in this case, Aaron – and talk through the crisis in their life that we’re going to talk about and how we’ll focus in on the feelings and emotions that challenge presented them with. Then, on the day, I’ll conduct the interview on camera and, afterwards, help with the edit, to get the story down to an accessible and powerful five or six minutes.

“Each of the Stories Like Ours is inspiring in its own way, with people remembering some of the most difficult and challenging moments they’ve lived through and telling us how they started to find a way past them. It’s humbling that people like Aaron are ready to trust us with their stories.

“I was really happy with how Aaron’s film turned out. The Stories Like Ours only achieve their objective, though, when they’re watched, talked about and thought about by the young people we’re aiming to reach with them.

“Aaron’s film and the other Stories Like Ours are available free to any organisation working with young people. The films aim to start conversations around life challenges and the feelings and emotions which those experiences involve. They’re being trialled in schools, prisons, sports academies and on community projects in Islington and across the country.

“So far, feedback is that young people are finding the films both watchable and thought-provoking, and that session organisers are able to use them to jump into having some difficult and important conversations.”
Aaron Barker is 32 and from London. He is the subject of a hard-hitting story about how he turned his life around…

“The film tells the story of my early life. In short, I was taken into care, selling drugs at 14 and getting into gang fights. At 16 I was attacked and stabbed, suffering nine puncture wounds plus slashes and cuts. At 16 I was all over the place emotionally and mentally, and I didn’t have the emotional intelligence to articulate my feelings. Now, something that I carry with me is that I know you always have a choice in life.

“Since I endured those experiences in my adolescent years, I detached myself from the negative aspects and I have gone on to complete and undergraduate and masters course. I’m now a professional quantity surveyor working in the construction industry on a mixture of residential/commercial and civil engineering projects.

“I first met Les as a teenager when I was under the care of Islington council. We reconnected in my adult years via a former colleague of his and we’ve remained in contact since. I’ve always wanted to give back in someway and this seemed like the perfect opportunity.
“In the film I spoke from the heart so there was no script as such, but Tom assisted with the location because football is so close to my heart.

“I’d never done anything like this before so I was a tad nervous, but the film crew’s reaction filled me with confidence. I was really happy with the result and I trust Les and Tom will do their best with it.

“I just hope that my story can in some way helped or inspire others. I was blessed to encounter people and experiences along my way that have helped to guide and influence my life. If my story can help even individual think differently or give them an alternative perspective I will be happy.”

There are four Stories Like Ours so far but plans for many more over the coming months. Just contact Les at to find out how to get involved, either as a subject for a film or as a sponsor who can help us tell another story. You can watch Aaron’s story

items.summaryZh: 阿森纳基金会资助了ACED项目的一部纪实短片。
bodyZh: 阿森纳基金会资助了ACED项目“我们的故事”系列短片之一，讲述了亚伦（Aaron）在经历毒品和持刀袭击后重塑人生的真实故事。该片背后的三位核心人物——莱斯·罗、汤姆·沃特以及亚伦本人——向我们讲述了其中的经历。
莱斯·罗是ACED项目社区利益公司的董事，“我们的故事”系列短片正是在该公司旗下的伞形架构下制作的。他碰巧也是埃米尔·史密斯·罗的父亲……

“我与阿森纳社区部门的联系始于我在伊斯灵顿离家照料服务机构Independent Future担任教育、就业和培训顾问的角色。我与社区团队密切合作，为年轻人推荐就业和培训机会。我曾带孩子们参加街头儿童世界杯，并且每年圣诞节我都会与社区团队及一家名为‘向前青年’的慈善机构在阿森纳中心合作，为离家照料的年轻人举办圣诞午餐。我一直希望埃米尔保持低调，所以他也参加过该活动以及我们在中心的‘开球’家庭作业俱乐部。”
“ACED项目社区利益公司源于2021年封城期间在领英上的一次偶然对话，当时志同道合的人们热切希望利用体育——特别是足球的力量——来支持有照料经历的年轻人。我们的目标是让这个群体‘心怀远大、协同合作并被赋能’，这也是我们名称的由来。我的同事董事、父子组合布拉德利和杰克·戈尔德伯格以及我本人，与广泛的组织合作开展项目，旨在激励年轻人并帮助他们找到工作或获得资格证书。”
“汤姆和我是在阿森纳中心对面的一家咖啡馆认识的。我当时正要去酋长球场观看一场青年队的比赛，便顺路进去喝杯咖啡。我看到汤姆坐在那里，由于从他在《东区人》中的角色认出了他，便想着打个招呼。”
“汤姆非常平易近人，我们坐在一起聊了一会儿足球，然后我才透露我去球场的目的。汤姆对埃米尔赞不绝口，称他是每个人都在关注的年轻球员之一。从那以后我们一直保持联系，现在在‘我们的故事’项目上紧密合作。”
“制作这些短片完全依赖于捐赠。我很幸运能有一位长期朋友赞助了第一片，而阿森纳中心的一名青训梯队球员家长赞助了第二部。阿森纳基金会则帮助我们完成了第四部短片。”
汤姆·沃特是“我们的故事”的采访者和导演，他做阿森纳球迷已有近60年之久……
“1986年，我遇到了艾伦·塞夫顿，他是我的足球英雄之一，当时他来到海布里担任阿森纳第一任社区主管。我很幸运能从那时起一直参与社区部门的工作，从为双重俱乐部计划制作教育材料——该计划正在庆祝其25周年——到创立阿森纳慈善足球队。这是一种荣幸和特权。现在，我很感激阿森纳基金会帮助我们将一个精彩的故事搬上银幕。”
“莱斯和一位同事正在筹建ACED项目，并正在寻找创意。我有一个主意：‘我们的故事’。从那以后，我们一直合作至今。”
“我与每部短片的传主坐在一起——本案中是亚伦——探讨他们生活中的危机以及我们将如何聚焦于该挑战给他们带来的感受和情感。然后，在拍摄当天，我会在镜头前进行采访，并在事后协助剪辑，将故事浓缩为易于理解且富有力量感的五到六分钟。”
“‘我们的故事’中的每一个故事都有其独特的启发性，人们回忆起他们经历过的一些最困难和最具挑战性的时刻，并告诉我们他们是如何开始找到克服这些困难的方法的。亚伦这样的人愿意把他们的故事托付给我们，这让我们感到谦卑。”
“我对亚伦的成片效果感到非常高兴。然而，只有当我们的短片被我们希望触及的年轻人观看、谈论和思考时，‘我们的故事’才能实现其目标。”
“亚伦的短片和其他‘我们的故事’短片可供任何致力于青少年工作的组织免费使用。这些短片旨在引发围绕生活挑战以及这些经历所涉及的感受和情感的对话。它们正在伊斯灵顿及全国各地的学校、监狱、体育学院和社区项目中进行试播。”
“到目前为止，反馈表明年轻人发现这些短片既具观赏性又引人深思，且活动组织者能够利用它们来展开一些困难而重要的对话。”
亚伦·巴克今年32岁，来自伦敦。他是这个关于他如何扭转人生的重磅故事的主角……
“这部短片讲述了我早年生活的故事。简而言之，我被送到照料机构，14岁开始卖毒品并卷入帮派斗殴。16岁时我遭到袭击并被刺伤，身受九处穿刺伤以及割伤和划伤。16岁时我在情感和精神上陷入混乱，并不具备表达自己感受的情商。现在，我随身携带的一个信念是：你知道生活中永远有选择。”
“自从在青春期经历了那些经历后，我将自己与负面因素剥离，并继续完成了本科和硕士课程。我现在是一名专业的工料测量师，在建筑行业从事住宅、商业和土木工程混合项目的工作。”
“我十几岁时在伊斯灵顿市议会的照料下第一次认识莱斯。成年后，我通过他的一位前同事与他重新取得了联系，并一直保持着联系。我一直想以某种方式回馈社会，而这似乎是一个完美的契机。”
“在片中我是发自内心地诉说，所以没有剧本可言，但汤姆协助选定了拍摄地点，因为足球对我而言意义深重。”
“我从未做过类似的事情，所以难免有些紧张，但摄制组的反应让我充满了信心。我对结果非常满意，并且相信莱斯和汤姆会尽最大努力处理好它。”
“我只希望我的故事能以某种方式帮助或启发他人。我很幸运在人生道路上遇到了能够指导和影响我生活的人与经历。如果我的故事能让哪怕一个人改变思维方式或提供另一种视角，我就会感到高兴。”
目前已有四部“我们的故事”，并且计划在未来几个月内推出更多作品。只需联系莱斯了解如何参与，无论是作为短片传主还是作为赞助商帮助我们讲述另一个故事。你可以观看亚伦的故事

items.summaryEn: Ahead of Arsenal's Champions League match against Monaco, we look back at some of the club's best goals against Ligue 1 sides
bodyEn: We’ve looked back through the archives and selected some of our favourite goals against Ligue 1 clubs.
The Gunners have netted some delightful finishes against sides across the channel over the years, and these are just some of our top picks.

Jack WilshereArsenal 2-0 MarseilleNovember 26, 2013What a start - and what a finish! It took Jack Wilshere precisely 28 seconds to give Arsenal the lead in this Champions League group stage match against Marseille during the 2013/14 season.

Starting on the right side of Arsenal’s midfield, Wilshere took advantage of the visitors’ high defensive line to latch onto Bacary Sagna’s pass down the wing. The England midfielder charged towards the byline, feinted one way and then cut inside before curling the ball sumptuously beyond Steve Mandanda and into the top corner.
Wilshere, enjoying one of his best displays of the season, made sure of three points in the second half, calmly slotting home from Mesut Ozil’s inviting low centre.

The Gunners went on to progress from Group F after a nerve-shredding defeat at Napoli on matchday six - the Italian team was incredibly eliminated from the tournament because of an inferior head-to-head record despite collecting 12 points, the same amount as Borussia Dortmund, who topped the group, and Arsenal.
Lukas PodolskiArsenal 2-0 MontpellierNovember 21, 2012Lukas Podolski could scarcely have ensured qualification to the last 16 of the 2012/13 Champions League in a more emphatic way.

With Arsenal leading 1-0 against Montpellier thanks to Jack Wilshere’s delicate dink, the German international secured three points with a stunning 63rd-minute volley. Playing a one-two with Olivier Giroud, Podolski ran on to the aerial return pass and powered a trademark volley into the roof of the net from just inside the area. Visiting goalkeeper Geoffrey Jourdren had no chance.

Arsenal finished second in the group, securing a last-16 meeting with Bayern Munich. Having lost the first leg 3-1 at Emirates Stadium - a game in which Podolski was again on target - Olivier Giroud and Laurent Koscielny scored at Allianz Arena to give the Gunners a highly impressive 2-0 victory in the second leg. It wasn’t quite enough though, with Arsenal going out on away goals.

Thierry HenryLens 1-2 ArsenalApril 20, 2000This was classic Thierry Henry - scoring a vital goal at a crucial time in this UEFA Cup semi-final to set up Arsenal’s passage to a meeting with Galatasaray in Copenhagen.
Dennis Bergkamp’s early strike had secured a 1-0 victory in the first leg at Highbury, but this would be a very different test for Arsène Wenger’s men.

Henry, who had already scored six goals in the competition that season, had initially been well marshalled in the return match, often surrounded by defenders keen to snap into challenges whenever he received the ball.

But just before half-time, Arsenal’s record goalscorer doubled the aggregate lead with a goal of top class. Receiving the ball with his back to goal on the left-hand side of the area, Henry held off his man, turned quickly and lashed a shot into the corner.
Pascal Nouma did equalise after the break but Kanu ensured Arsenal’s place in the final three minutes from time.

Dennis BergkampArsenal 1-1 LyonFebruary 21, 2001Dennis Bergkamp at his best - strong, composed, easy on the eye and making the difficult look oh so simple. Racing onto Robert Pires’ pass, the Iceman shrugged off a covering defender with ease, advanced into the box and calmly opened his body to send a shot right into the top corner.

Edmilson’s late equaliser initially prevented the goal from helping Arsenal to qualify from the second group stage of the Champions League - though they eventually did, the 1-0 victory in this reverse fixture ensuring Arsène Wenger’s men went through after both teams finished with eight points.
Arsenal were knocked out by Valencia on away goals in the quarter-finals.
Nigel WinterburnArsenal 3-0 NantesNovember 25, 1999Arsenal entered the Uefa Cup after finishing third in a tricky Champions League group, behind Barcelona and Fiorentina.
Their first opponents in the tournament were French side Nantes. who were comfortably beaten in the first leg of this third-round tie on a chilly November night at Highbury.

Marc Overmars’ penalty had put the hosts in command before Nigel Winterburn added a thunderous late second. Receiving the ball from Patrick Vieira just outside the left side of the penalty area, the full back took a touch to set himself before unleashing a powerful swerving effort that flew into the corner of the goal.
It was Winterburn’s first European goal - and one that commentator Martin Tyler described as “fabulous”.
Dennis Bergkamp added further gloss to the score and Arsenal drew the return match 3-3 before going on to reach the final of the competition, eventually losing to Galatasaray on penalties.

items.summaryZh: 阿森纳对阵摩纳哥欧冠赛前，回顾队史对阵法甲球队的精彩进球。
bodyZh: 我们翻阅了历史资料，挑选了一些我们最喜欢的对阵法甲俱乐部的进球。
多年来，阿森纳在面对海峡对岸的球队时打入了一些精妙的进球，以下只是我们精选的一部分。
杰克·威尔希尔，阿森纳 2-0 马赛，2013年11月26日，多么完美的开局，多么精彩的进球！在2013/14赛季这场对阵马赛的欧冠小组赛中，杰克·威尔希尔仅用了28秒就为阿森纳首开纪录。
威尔希尔从阿森纳右侧中场启动，利用客队的高位防线，接住了萨尼亚沿边路的传球。这位英格兰中场带球冲向底线，先是假动作晃过对手随后内切，接着用一记美妙的弧线球将球送入斯特沃·曼丹达把守球门的死角。
威尔希尔奉献了本赛季最佳表现之一，他在下半场接厄齐尔精妙的低平球传中冷静推射破门，锁定胜局。
在第六轮客场负于那不勒斯经历惊心动魄的比赛后，枪手顺利从F组出线——尽管意大利球队与多特蒙德（小组第一）和阿森纳同积12分，但因相互交手战绩处于劣势而被淘汰出局。
卢卡斯·波多尔斯基，阿森纳 2-0 蒙彼利埃，2012年11月21日，卢卡斯·波多尔斯基以一种极具说服力的方式确保了阿森纳晋级2012/13赛季欧冠十六强。
凭借杰克·威尔希尔精巧的挑射，阿森纳当时以1-0领先蒙彼利埃，随后这位德国国脚在第63分钟以一记精彩的凌空抽射锁定胜局。波多尔斯基与吉鲁完成撞墙配合，迎着空中回传的皮球，在禁区边缘标志性地迎球怒射，皮球直飞网窝。客队门将戈弗雷·茹尔德伦毫无机会。
阿森纳在小组中排名第二，在十六强赛中遭遇拜仁慕尼黑。首回合在酋长球场以1-3失利（波多尔斯基在那场比赛中再次进球），随后吉鲁和科斯切尔尼在安联球场破门，帮助枪手在次回合取得令人印象深刻的2-0胜利。不过这还不够，阿森纳最终因客场进球劣势出局。
蒂埃里·亨利，朗斯 1-2 阿森纳，2000年4月20日，这是典型的蒂埃里·亨利——在这场联盟杯半决赛的关键时刻打入关键进球，为阿森纳进军哥本哈根对阵加拉塔萨雷铺平了道路。
丹尼斯·博格帕克的早期进球确保了海布里首回合1-0的胜利，但对温格的球队来说，这将是一场截然不同的考验。
亨利当赛季在该赛事中已经攻入六球，在次回合比赛中起初受到严密盯防，每当他拿球时总有防守球员蜂拥而至。
但在半场结束前，阿森纳的历史最佳射手用一个世界级进球将总比分优势扩大了一倍。亨利在禁区左侧背对球门接球，顶住防守球员，快速转身并起脚怒射破门得分。
帕斯卡尔·努马在下半场扳平比分，但卡努在比赛还剩三分钟时确保了阿森纳晋级决赛。
丹尼斯·博格坎普，阿森纳 1-1 里昂，2001年2月21日，巅峰时期的丹尼斯·博格坎普——强壮、沉稳、赏心悦目，将高难度动作做得如此简单。冰王子接罗伯特·皮雷的传球后轻松甩开补防的防守球员，突入禁区，冷静舒展身体将球直接送入死角。
埃德米尔森随后的扳平进球起初阻碍了该进球帮助阿森纳从欧冠第二阶段小组赛出线——尽管他们最终还是晋级了，双方均积8分，而这场次回合的1-0胜利确保了温格的球队顺利过关。
阿森纳在四分之一决赛中因客场进球劣势被瓦伦西亚淘汰。
奈杰尔·温特本，阿森纳 3-0 南特，1999年11月25日，阿森纳在艰难的欧冠小组赛中名列巴塞罗那和佛罗伦萨之后获得第三名，从而进入联盟杯。
他们在该赛事中的首个对手是法甲球队南特，在一个寒冷的11月夜晚的海布里球场，他们在第三轮首回合比赛中轻松取胜。
马克·奥弗马斯的点球让主队占据优势，随后奈杰尔·温特本在尾声阶段轰入一记精彩的世界波。这位边后卫接帕特里克·维埃拉在禁区左侧外沿的传球，调整了一步后起脚轰出一记势大力沉且带有弧线的远射，皮球飞入球门死角。
这是温特本的第一粒欧战进球——解说员马丁·泰勒将其形容为“美妙绝伦”。
丹尼斯·博格坎普锦上添花，阿森纳在次回合3-3战平对手，随后一路杀入赛事决赛，最终在点球大战中负于加拉塔萨雷。
